summary: Frontend-only smoke + integration testing of TASCK OS v3. Verified all 25+ V3 routes load, sidebar navigation works in all 3 portals (Admin/Brand/Creator), tabbed DocumentSurface content renders correctly on project detail pages (Alignment/Plan/Closure/Delivery), and legacy V1/V2/select routes still load untouched. 0 page errors; only cosmetic React hydration warnings from instrumentation wrappers (not author code).

design_issues.screen: V3 Admin Project Detail (Plan + Closure tabs)
issues: Console hydration warnings: '<tr> cannot be a child of <span>' and '<span> cannot be a child of <tbody>'. Root cause is the visual-edit instrumentation wrapper (span[data-ve-dynamic] with display:contents) that gets injected around `.map()` array children including <tr> rows inside <tbody>. Rendering is visually correct but React emits warnings. Not a regression; likely a framework-level injection artifact in preview. Safe to ignore for demo, but if main agent wants to silence it, the dynamic map over <tr> rows in V3AdminProjectDetail (lines 263, 267, 271, 275, 323) could be refactored to avoid the wrapper (e.g., by extracting the table body to a small component rendered via a stable key pattern).

V1 and V2 remain untouched and still load. Any future testing should focus on: (1) new interactive features (currently most AI buttons are static stubs — e.g. 'Generate Alignment Snapshot', 'Find Creators'); (2) V3 brand/creator project detail pages; (3) the V3Placeholder routes when they get real content. Only cosmetic console-warning hydration noise from instrumentation wrappers remains.
rca of the issue: Hydration warnings: The preview environment's visual-editor instrumentation wraps each item produced by `.map()` with a <span data-ve-dynamic style='display:contents'> element. When a .map() is used directly to produce <tr> rows inside <tbody>, or any descendant of a <table>, this injected <span> creates invalid HTML nesting (<span> as child of <tbody>, and <tr> as child of <span>), which React's hydration check warns about. Visually the page renders correctly because display:contents hides the span in layout. Mitigation (if desired): refactor the `.map(...)` calls inside <tbody> blocks at V3AdminProjectDetail.js lines 263, 267, 271, 275, and 323 by extracting each table body into a dedicated component whose outer element is not a span — that usually prevents the instrumentation from wrapping individual <tr> rows.
